business_scope.primary_industry_name: Real-Time Video Matching and Cross-Border Social Telephony

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition; unitary national legal system with no sub-state company law distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (entered into force 1995)
France–People's Republic of China DTA (entered into force 2014)
France–Hong Kong SAR DTA (entered into force 2010)
Agreement between France and the United Arab Emirates on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1995)
EU internal market freedoms (Articles 49 and 54 TFEU) applicable to EEA/EU shareholders
France–China BIT (signed 1984; renegotiated, terminated for intra-EU only, remains applicable to Chinese investors)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-50 and R. 561-1 et seq.; Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 (transposing EU Directive 2015/849/AMLD4 as amended); Décret n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018 (RBE filing to the registre du commerce et des sociétés); Loi n° 2020-1508 of 3 December 2020 (transposition of AMLD5); Code de commerce Articles L. 123-1, L. 123-11-1 and L. 561-45; Article 1649 bis C of the Code général des impôts (obligatory UBO statement to the tax administration); ACPR and AMF guidance on AML/CFT for digital activities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of each non-French corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of country of origin (e.g., UAE Ministry of Economy / DMCC Registrar, Hong Kong Companies Registry, US Secretary of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (issuing state party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise French Consular Legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each UBO and each SARL manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of UBO's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or notarized copy certified by a French consular officer (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (dated utility bill or municipal attestation issued within last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or municipal registry of UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each UBO (confirming identity, signature, and professional history)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the UBO (authorized officer signatory)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for each non-French shareholder authorizing the French incorporator to sign the constitution file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Articles of Association (statuts) of the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French civil-law notaire (if acte notarié) or incorporated counsel under signature privée countersigned by the notaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct notarial certification (no apostille required for domestic French act)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening standards: All UBOs, managers, and authorized signatories must be screened against (i) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (ii) French national asset-freezing measures (Direction générale du Trésor – AVI list); (iii) OFAC SDN List; (iv) UN Security Council consolidated list; (v) FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions list; and (vi) French FIU (Tracfin) supervision guidance. PEP status is determined per FATF Recommendation 12 and CMF Articles L. 561-10 and R. 561-18 to R. 561-20. Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification of the video-chat social app segment, enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory, including source-of-wealth verification for PEPs and documentary confirmation of the origin of funds; continuous adverse-media and sanctions monitoring is required post-incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises – INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); name verification via the INPI corporate data portal (data.inpi.fr) and the RCS database operated by Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin alphabet characters; where the chosen name is in a foreign script or language it must be transliterated into Latin script and accompanied by a French version in the statuts. The name must not be contrary to French public policy or morality (Code de commerce Article L. 123-1(7)). French is the operative language for all documents filed with the greffe; non-French annexes require certified translation by a sworn translator (traducteur assermenté).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a formal name pre-reservation system; the name is effectively cleared at the moment the constitution file is submitted to the Guichet Unique. If the INPI or the competent greffe rejects the proposed name (identity, similarity, or prohibited token ground), counsel shall (i) obtain the written rejection grounds; (ii) file an administrative complaint via the same INPI portal within 15 days; (iii) alternatively refile with a modified and duly re-screened name within 48–72 hours; (iv) if the rejection is grounded in a third-party trademark, initiate a voluntary amendment of the statuts or, if commercially justified, obtain a coexistence letter; and (v) for unlawful refusals, petition the President of the commercial court (tribunal de commerce) in référé for an order compelling registration, with costs recoverable against the registry in the event of gross negligence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the first five (5) years of operation exclusively through a duly approved third-party domiciliation provider registered with the Regional Chamber of Commerce and the greffe (Code de commerce Article L. 123-11-1). The domiciliation provider must have physical premises in France and must be registered under the special authorisation regime. This is commercially acceptable for the video-matching app business because the activity is digital and has no retail footprint; however, from year six a physical office in France is mandatory. Business bank accounts (including neobanks such as Qonto) will accept an approved domiciliation address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – estimated 3% probability of unannounced on-site inspection within the first three (3) years of operation, given the non-regulated, digital-only nature of the activity. Unplanned inspections by URSSAF, tax auditors, or Tracfin are typically triggered by payroll activity, inconsistent UBO filings, or suspicious transaction reports, none of which are baseline expectations for this structure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel fees – SARL constitution file (drafting statuts, governance charter, UBO statement, RCS appendices, AML/CFT file review)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cross-border corporate law firm / French avocat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (€1,200–€1,800) for standard SARL formation with foreign shareholders and English/French bilingual documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet Unique / INPI filing and RCS registration legal tax (taxe sur les actes, droit d'enregistrement and greffe fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and greffe du tribunal de commerce (collected via Guichet Unique)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (frais de greffe per Article R. 123-211 of the Code de commerce and applicable décret)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication légale – incorporation notice in an approved Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered legal gazette (e.g., Les Affiches Parisiennes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated competitive market rate, range €180–€260 per publication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille authentication of foreign UBO corporate and identity documents (3 documents @ $50 per apostille)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the issuing state (e.g., UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Hong Kong High Court, US Secretary of State)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per apostille set by the issuing state; $50 average

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translation of apostilled foreign documents (approx. 5 pages @ $60/page)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Traducteur expert assermenté près la cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing tariff of the Cour d'appel approved translators, €45–€65 per standard page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fees for optional acte notarié and signature legalization of the statuts (if required by foreign shareholder or tax authority)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compagnie des notaires de Paris / relevant French notariat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed tariff (tarif réglementé) for notarial acts, range €400–€600

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Third-party domiciliation agreement (registered office at an approved French business domiciliation provider) – 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation provider registered with the CCI (e.g., Regus or equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark €55–€85 per month for a Paris or major-city approved domicile

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO and AML compliance screening pack – PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and French sanctions lists plus adverse media and litigation database check for all UBOs/managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent AML/CFT compliance counsel (enhanced due diligence provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Medium_Risk_Enhanced EDD of up to three (3) UBOs, including database subscriptions and counsel review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability, trademark pre-clearance and RCS conflict search (INPI data portal + Infogreffe search)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and delegated IP/trademark search firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; INPI trademark search official fee €0–€40 plus delegate search fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve – courier / apostille delivery, consular appointments, bank AML questionnaire witness fees and EDD document certification

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (France), Book II Title III: Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-26 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Decree n°2007-111 of 22 May 2007; Articles 1834-1844-13 of the Civil Code are not applicable to SARL articles unless expressly referred to.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) accessible through the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises / Infogreffe online portal; final registration is performed by the Greffe which issues the Extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (Cerfa n°14795-07) — Declaration of Incorporation of a Commercial Company, accompanied by the signed recapitalized Articles of Association (Statuts) in French and the capital deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL has no statutory minimum capital; the articles can fix any amount in euros with a minimum nominal share value of EUR 1. However, every cash contribution must be fully paid at incorporation and deposited into a blocked bank account (or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations) before filing. The blocked-funds certificate is released after registration and the Gérant may not withdraw funds prior to issuance of the Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [SARL NAME] — Adopted on [date] by the shareholders holding 100% of the issued shares. RESOLVED: (1) the subscriptions to the share capital, as listed in the articles of association, are hereby approved, and the shares are fully paid up; (2) the registered office located at [address] is adopted as the legal seat of the company until board determines otherwise; (3) [GÉRANT NAME] is appointed as Gérant, sole officer, with full corporate representation and management powers; (4) the Gérant is authorised to execute all CFE/Greffe filings, pay all statutory fees, and obtain the Extrait Kbis. The resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All shareholders (associés) acting collectively; optional notarial assistance if contributions in kind or several shareholders require notaire certification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language Statuts containing the corporate name, legal form (SARL), registered office, corporate purpose (video matching and social telephony services), duration (99 years), share capital, number of shares and nominal value, rights attached to shares, management powers of the Gérant(s), annual meetings, and arbitration rules. Each shareholder must sign every copy of the Statuts. For un-notarized private deeds, handwrite 'lu et approuvé' with signature and initial page. Deliver authenticated copies to all parties.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts in French
Identity proof of each shareholder (passport / ID card)
Proof of address of each shareholder
Notarized power of attorney if a shareholder signs by proxy
Proof of right to use the future registered office (not required at this stage but prepared)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder or notary identifies a legal inconsistency in the bylaws, hold an immediate ad hoc assembly and execute a corrective amendment (avenant). Where a notary refuses certification because the object is unlawful, revise the corporate object to fit within ISIC 6311/NAICS 519130 categories and not serve regulated activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Capital Deposit and Escrow for Cash Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any bank established in France (chosen by the shareholders) or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) acting as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the name of the SARL in formation with the future Gérant as authorized signatory. Each shareholder transfers/remits their cash contribution into this blocked account with the reference 'capital souscrit [SARL NAME]' and obtains a bank receipt. The Bank/CDC issues the formal capital-deposit certificate ('attestation de dépôt des fonds') stating the full amount subscribed and confirming that the funds are blocked until production of the registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts
Board/shareholder decision appointing the Gérant for purposes of opening the account
Identity documents of the Gérant and any co-signatories
Amount breakdown per shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays issuing the attestation, request in writing a justification; if the bank refuses, terminate that account and open an escrow account with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations. Non-remittance by a shareholder is a default on subscription, and the shareholder may be replaced by a new subscriber under the terms of the Statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Announcement (Avis de constitution) in an Authorized Legal Journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A 'Journal d'Annonces Légales' (JAL) approved by the Prefecture in the département where the registered office is located; list accessible in the préfecture/Greffe.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the legal announcement in French, covering corporate name, form 'SARL', capital amount, registered office, purpose, duration, the Gérant(s) name(s), and the commercial court for registration (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce). Send the text to the selected JAL with the order and payment. Obtain the 'justificatif de parution' (certificate of publication) no later than the registration filing date. The publication must be done before or on the same day as filing the M0.
required_dossiers: Project of Statuts or a summary certified by the shareholder(s)
Declaration of the registered office address
Identification of the Gérant(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL is not approved by the Prefecture or publishes the announcement on the day of the refusal, select another newspaper from the official JAL list, pay the new fee and publish on the same or next business day. If the publication certificate contains typographical errors, request a corrective 'rectificatif' insertion immediately so that the registry does not reject the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Registration File through CFE/Infogreffe and Payment of the Registry Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) — selected Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce or Infogreffe online filing portal (www.infogreffe.fr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 declaration (Cerfa 14795-07) in French, add the beneficial-owner declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs), attach the Statuts signed, the capital attestation, the legal-publication certificate, a proof of authority over the registered office (lease or letter of use), identity cards of the Gérant, and powers of attorney if signed by proxy. File electronically via Infogreffe; pay the civil and registration duty (approximated USD 95). The CFE will transmit the file to the greffe; keep the timestamped récépissé as evidence of timely filing.
required_dossiers: Formulaire M0 (Cerfa n°14795-07) signed
Signed articles of association (Statuts)
Capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Legal publication certificate (justificatif de parution)
Proof of occupancy / lease or right to use the registered office
Identity document of the Gérant(s)
Declarations des bénéficiaires effectifs
Power of attorney if the M0 is signed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a 'décision de refus' or asks for supplementary documents, the applicant must comply within the shortest statutorily permitted delay (usually 15 days). If the refusal is unjustified, petition the President of the Tribunal de Commerce using a complainte au juge commis à la surveillance in accordance with Articles R.123-92-1 et seq. of the Code de commerce. Re-delivery of any missing document via Infogreffe resumes the process and does not reset the priority of the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Verification and Board Governance Kick-off
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INSEE (registration notified automatically to SIRENE database).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Greffe completes registration, retrieve the official 'Extrait Kbis' (certificate of incorporation), SIREN, SIRET and code APE (6311A / or 6311B as assigned). Ensure the Gérant performs the corporation's first legal compliance actions: open a corporate bank account, apply for VAT and ID provisions from the tax administration (via auto-created SIREN), and place mandatory notice of Kbis in the registered office. Update the internal shareholder register. Record the final board minutes.
required_dossiers: No additional dossiers are required from the company; the Greffe automatically generates the Extrait Kbis and INSEE notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Extrait Kbis contains any data mismatch (e.g., registered office, manager name), send a rectification request to the Greffe within one week and, upon persistent error, file a motion with the President of the Commercial Court under R.123-87 to force correction. If SIRET is delayed, you can request the SIRENE code directly from INSEE using the Kbis extract.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; digital 'real-time video matching and social telephony' is not an industrial activity requiring an installation permit. For any leased office premises, the local Mairie (through the urbanisme department) may issue an occupancy/commercialisation declaration only if the premises are open to the public or are materially altered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required at the national stage. The company must, however, file the declaration provided for in Article L.33-1 of the Code des Postes et des Communications Électroniques with the Autorité de régulation des communications électroniques, des postes et de la distribution de la presse (ARCEP) if it is deemed to be an operator of an electronic communications service genuinely open to the public. The purely interactive video-chat functionality usually falls outside traditional telephony licensing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL — Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (under the Ministry for Ecological Transition) is the main EIA agency for physical installations; the SARL is also subject to CNIL requirements for personal-data handling (notably practice of the video-match dataset).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (REMP/Registration not required) — no EIA is applicable to a serverless software-as-a-service application without production facilities, physical industrial installations, or waste-producing processes. At-most office IT equipment is covered by the WEEE and electronic-equipment disposal obligations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No threshold applies to wastewater, VOCs or atmospheric effluents. Should servers be operated separately, the data centers would be subject to EU Code of Conduct standards; for the office, general waste must be sorted and disposed under the Code de l'environnement, with e-waste in 'DEEE' channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No mandatory fire-safety certificate applies to a pure digital company until a physical office is opened. If an office is used, the employer must perform an initial occupational health and safety inspection under Articles R.4227-1 et seq. of the Code du travail, install fire extinguishers, maintain an updated 'registre unique du personnel', and receive a non-ERP occupational occupancy document from the insurance company. If more than 300 persons are present or the office is open to the public, a fire-safety permit from the Commission de Sécurité (classified ERP) would be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), the French national tax administration operating through impots.gouv.fr; company formation and initial tax identity are processed electronically by the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) under the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Established SARL: registration of the company at the RCS via the Guichet Unique automatically generates a SIREN/SIRET; DGFiP then assigns the French intra-Community VAT number (FR + 9 digits) without any separate filing. Non-established foreign digital operator with French taxable supplies and no PE: application for direct VAT registration must be made to the DGFiP Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), including the designation of an accredited fiscal representative where required; alternatively, the EU/non-EU One-Stop Shop (OSS) regimes may cover EU B2C digital services without a French VAT registration. No payment of minimum capital or license is required for the SARL (CGI non-resident ownership permitted).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box system. The SARL is an opaque legal entity default-taxed at corporate level: profits are subject to corporation tax ('impôt sur les sociétés' – IS) under CGI art. 206, with territoriality under CGI art. 209 confining IS to French-sourced/PE-attributable operations. Statutory elections: (i) qualifying small SARLs (unlisted, at least 50% of capital held by individuals and fewer than 50 employees) may elect, under CGI art. 239 bis AA, to be taxed as a transparent partnership for a non-renewable five-year period; (ii) sociétés civiles and family companies may rely on art. 239 bis A transparency in specific cases; (iii) ATAD 2 anti-hybrid matching rules (CGI arts. 209 I quinquies and 212 bis) re-characterize hybrid transparent/opaque mismatches and deny deductions for structured arrangements, meaning a US-style check-the-box election cannot be imported into France.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA) under CGI arts. 256 to 289, aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover registration threshold for an SARL established in France: the company is taxable from its first euro of economic activity (CGI arts. 256 and 286). A small established business may, however, benefit from the franchise en base de TVA exemption if annual service turnover does not exceed approximately EUR 36,300 (tolerance up to EUR 40,300) or goods turnover approximately EUR 91,000 (tolerance up to EUR 101,000), indexed annually; this exemption is irrelevant for the digital app because the SARL is created for taxable platform activity and Apple IAP/Paymentwall volumes will exceed the thresholds. Non-established foreign suppliers of digital services are registrable from the first euro unless the OSS is used.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France imposes a full e-invoicing and e-reporting reform: as legislated, all B2B e-invoices for VAT-taxable persons established in France must be issued and transmitted digitally through certified Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs) or the public state platform (Portail Public de Facturation – PPF) with mandatory structured formats (Factur-X hybrid XML/PDF, UBL 2.1, or UN/CEFACT CII). Phased enforcement: 1 September 2026 for large/mid-market enterprises; 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises. The PPF operates a 'Y'-architecture data exchange with State slots and public APIs for direct submission, invoice acceptance/rejection, interruption/outage management and the mandatory audit trail; transaction and payment data for B2C (including digital app sales) are also mandatorily reported (e-reporting) at least monthly, no later than the 10th day of the following month, to the DGFiP through the same certified channels. French law does not use the 'digital stamp' clearance model; instead it combines pre-authorized certification, API-based transmission, and NF 525 certification for cash-register/billing software (applicable to any French billing tool used for the app's payment rails). Non-compliant invoicing is penalized under CGI arts. 1737 and 1737 ter.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: exports of tangible goods outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT under CGI art. 262 ter I provided the goods physically leave the EU within 90 days (12 months for justified specific movements) and the exporter holds contemporaneous export proof; intra-EU supplies to VAT-registered customers are exempt with right to deduct under art. 262 ter II, subject to reverse charge in the destination Member State. Digital services of the app: the SARL's supplies to B2B customers outside France (EU or non-EU) are outside French VAT by place-of-supply rule (CGI art. 259 A; art. 44 VAT Directive) and are invoiced without 20% VAT if two corroborating proofs of business establishment are retained (valid VAT ID, business address, contract, bank details). B2C supplies to EU consumers are taxed in the consumer's Member State and reported via the OSS portal of the DGFiP; B2C supplies to non-EU consumers are outside French VAT if customer-residence evidence (IP geolocation, billing country, payment records) is kept. Marketplaces/deemed supplier: when Apple App Store (Apple IAP) qualifies as an app-store operator, Apple is deemed to have received the SARL's digital service and to re-supply it to the consumer under VAT Directive art. 14a, so the SARL issues a zero-rated B2B invoice to Apple and Apple accounts for consumer VAT; Paymentwall acts solely as payment intermediary and does not change the place-of-supply analysis.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation, DAU screen/ECS) validated by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN), evidencing departure from EU customs territory.

Commercial invoice and delivery/supply log, describing the goods or the digital service performed, the counterparty, the consideration, and citing the VAT exemption provision (CGI art. 262 ter I or II, or place-of-supply rule).
Bill of Lading, CMR waybill or Air Waybill with customs transit documents proving physical exit from the EU.

Inward remittance evidence: bank SWIFT/MT103 credit advice or platform payout statement demonstrating receipt of the invoiced amount; France does not require a formal central-bank inward remittance certificate.

Digital service substantiation file: contract, IP-address geolocation logs, OSS/ViES validation records, Apple iTunes Connect payment reports and Paymentwall settlement statements identifying the customer/residence.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French tax and customs auditors (vérification de comptabilité) may reassess incorrectly zero-rated exports within the standard three-year limitation period (LPF art. L. 174), extended to six years where the taxpayer has been guilty of fraud or serious tax offence. Retroactive clawbacks apply in full with intérêts de retard (CGI art. 1727) of 0.20% per month. Quantitative penalties: 40% for deliberate bad faith (mauvaise foi) and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers (manoeuvres frauduleuses) under CGI art. 1729; incomplete or false invoicing attracts separate fines under art. 1737. Criminal exposure: art. 1741 CGI treats fictitious exports/fake zero-rating as tax fraud, carrying a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and up to 5 years' imprisonment (increased to EUR 1,000,000 and 7 years for aggravated cases), plus confiscation, publication of the decision, and joint and several liability of any participant in the fraudulent chain under CGI art. 283(4).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as the national central bank within the Eurosystem/ESCB and as the sole administrator of French balance-of-payments (RFE) declarations; foreign-exchange and capital-movement policy is co-administered by the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury, Ministry of Economy and Finance); banking prudential supervision and AML oversight is exercised by the ACPR (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution), an independent authority attached to the Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible on both current account and capital account for French residents. Following the liberalisation of French exchange-control legislation (Decree 89-938 and the Finance Act 1989, subsequently embedded in the Code monétaire et financier, Articles L151-1 through L165-2, and in TFEU Article 63), a French SARL requires no prior exchange-control authorisation to receive foreign equity, to repatriate export-of-services proceeds, to pay foreign suppliers, or to distribute dividends to non-resident shareholders. Capital-account restrictions exist only in the targeted sectors listed by the decree on inward foreign investment (Defence, cybersecurity, critical infrastructure, space operations, chemical/biological/radiological/nuclear technologies); a real-time video-matching social app under ISIC 6311/NAICS 519130 is not a sensitive sector and is not subject to prior authorisation. Profit and dividend remittances to non-residents are legally free but carry practical hurdles: (i) the SARL's gérant must evidence a validly approved annual accounts and a shareholders' meeting decision; (ii) the distribution must respect the balance sheet solvency and legal-reserve rules of Code de commerce Articles L232-10 to L232-11; (iii) a dividend withholding tax applies to non-resident shareholders — 25% standard for a non-treaty resident corporate shareholder, 12.8% single income levy plus 17.2% social levies for natural persons when a tax-transparent regime applies, with rates reduced by double-taxation treaties (e.g., Bhutan, Hong Kong, US, Swiss, UK); and (iv) banking KYC expectations require traceability of the profit source, but there is no requirement to obtain an FX licence, a conversion permit, or a 'bona fide' certificate from the Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio. A French SARL may retain 100% of foreign-currency receipts in authorised foreign-currency accounts or convert them into EUR at market rates at any time; revenue from the video-matching app (Apple App Store and Paymentwall settlements) is classified as export of services for the purposes of the EU services trade and French statistics. The only statutory overlay is the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting regime: any French resident legal entity that executes a single transfer between France and a foreign country equal to or greater than EUR 7,500 — including export collections, import payments, capital subscriptions, and dividend flows — must declare the operation to the Banque de France under Regulation 91-07 and Directive of 5 September 1991 (Relations financières avec l'étranger, RFE), filed electronically through the TéléRFE portal within the prescribed monthly deadline, using the operation codes applicable to services (e.g., 'G2/Capi' for capital transactions; '1S' services for subscription-based app revenue). There is no requirement to convert proceeds, no minimum holding period, and no surrender certificate, and the EUR is the legal tender currency for the statutory accounts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium — acceptable as auxiliary rail, insufficient as the sole treasury anchor. French-regulated fintech EMIs (notably Qonto SAS, which holds an ACPR licence as an établissement de monnaie électronique and partners with French banking institutions; Shine as a subsidiary of Société Générale) are legally viable under Articles L521-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier for day-to-day operational accounts, card issuance, and open-API bookkeeping, and they allow fully remote onboarding even for foreign directors under eIDAS-compliant video KYC. However, for a cross-border video-matching app rated Medium_Risk_Enhanced, the following constraints apply: (i) SARL incorporation capital must be deposited in a blocked account held by an ACPR-licensed French credit institution or by a French notary (Code de commerce Article L223-7); an unlicensed or passporting-only foreign EMI cannot hold this statutory escrow; (ii) Banque de France RFE declarations are the client's responsibility and require bank statements with clear counterparty traceability, which passporting offshore EMIs (e.g., Wise European entity in Belgium, Revolut Lithuania, Airwallex/Currencycloud) may not emit with full French correspondent transparency; (iii) ACPR guidance disallows reliance on non-regulated e-money for long-term treasury of enhanced-risk digital companies; and (iv) foreign digital EMI platforms generally do not provide commercial credit lines, trade instruments, or FX hedging ISDA execution. Recommended architecture: anchor settlement liquidity and capital escrow with a Tier-1 bank (BNP Paribas or Société Générale) and use one EU-licensed EMI in parallel for low-value collection sweeps and payroll cards.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal statutory mandate that directors appear physically at the branch for every account; Article L561-5 of the Code monétaire et financier permits risk-based remote identification using eIDAS-certified electronic identity. In practice, however, ACPR-supervised Tier-1 banks (BNP Paribas, Société Générale, LCL, CIC) require at least one in-branch interview of the gérant (managing director), or exceptionally of a formally notarised attorney-in-fact, at account opening of a French SARL whose ultimate beneficial owners are non-residents or whose business is a cross-border consumer-facing digital app. The physical appearance can be waived by some branches if every director and UBO holds a valid EU/EEA passport, the SARL has a physical registered office with personnel, and the eKYC video verification is performed on a commercial platform recognized under the ACPR's digital onboarding doctrine. For a non-EU foreign-resident gérant (common in the described shareholder structure), the bank will typically demand: physical presence; a passport certified either by a French consulate or under apostille; certified French translation of the passport and residency proof; and a notarised statement of the UBOs. A remote-only opening should therefore be planned with a Medium-to-Low probability at the Tier-1 anchor bank; remote opening is highly probable at Qonto and other ACPR-licensed neobanks but only for the auxiliary account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Enhanced-risk digital business — a real-time random video-match application may be classified by the bank's first-line underwriting as a high-money-velocity platform exposed to romance-scam proceeds, unregulated micro-transactions, and mule-like payment pass-through via app-internal wallets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal business plan in French describing the matching algorithm, monetisation flows (Apple IAP, Paymentwall merchant ID), and absence of peer-to-peer internal wallet transfers; signed AML/CTF policy aligned with French Money Code Articles L561-1 et seq. and EU Regulation 2023/1113 (transfer of funds traceability); user and transaction monitoring documentation; DSA readiness statement (EC 2022/2065) with moderation and risk-management evidence; Paymentwall and Apple App Store merchant statements; 12-month volume forecast; proof of independence from any unregulated or anonymous payment vehicles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership — non-resident UBOs, nominee-shareholder structures, or a shareholder registered in a jurisdiction considered weak on AML/CFT will trigger refusal or enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified UBO declaration under Article L561-2-2 of the Code monétaire et financier; registration receipt of the registers of beneficial owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) with the Greffe du tribunal de commerce; passport copies of each UBO certified by a French consulate or apostilled; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence (bank statements, tax records, notarised declaration); full organisational chart showing the SARL's tiered ownership and capital path; sanctions-list screening report (EU, UN, OFAC).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow at incorporation — the SARL's share capital and share premium are contributed by foreign shareholders; banks must verify that none of the funds originate from cash, crypto-assets, or unregulated intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial attestation of capital blocking (attestation de blocage des fonds) if deposited with a notary, or a blocked-account certificate issued by a French credit institution under Article L223-7 of the Code de commerce; origin-of-funds letters from the transferring banks covering each shareholder; declaration that no cash/cryptocurrency was used; board resolution of the foreign shareholder approving the capital injection; transaction-reference mapping to the SARL's bank reference file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Domiciliation red flag — the SARL's registered office is at a commercial domiciliation provider (domiciliataire) which also hosts many unrelated shell-like companies, triggering suspicion of letterbox operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office lease or commercial domiciliation contract with a provider registered with CCI; physical presence plan (planned hires in France, registered payroll, equipment); employment/insurance documentation; location photographs and power-of-attorney deed; sworn statement of the gérant describing day-to-day management premises in France; utility bills evidencing operational presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Consumer-funds commingling and payment-aggregator concentration — the bank's AML model flags large incoming flows from Apple and Paymentwall whose underlying cardholders are unidentified to the bank, creating a 'pass-through vs treasury' ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete executed payment-provider contracts (Apple Developer Program License Agreement; Paymentwall Merchant Agreement) demonstrating that funds settle to the SARL's own bank account as merchant revenue, not as client money; reconciliation framework showing match between provider settlement reports and the SARL's ledger; signed treasury-management policy prohibiting co-mingling of consumer escrows; independent accountant's attestation on month-end settlement reconciliation; CNIL data-protection evidence if applicable; communication protocol to address the bank's regulatory interview on typologies including the prevalence of App Store refunds and chargebacks.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: equity capital for the French SARL (share capital plus share premium, if any) is wired by SWIFT MT103 (or Euro-system ISO 20022 pacs.008) from the foreign shareholder's bank into a blocked account (compte bloqué) held at a French ACPR-licensed credit institution, or into a notary's escrow account, with the field-70 remittance information stating 'Souscription au capital social — SARL [Entity Name] — RCS [town] — UBO [name] — application of Article L223-7 Code de commerce'. There is no prior exchange-control approval; France has removed prior-authorisation screening for this ISIC 6311 digital-services activity. The bank will execute the transfer to a French IBAN on the TARGET2 rail; once the SARL is registered on the RCS (K-bis extract issued), the bank unblocks the funds into the operational current account. Compliance duties: (a) for any single leg exceeding EUR 7,500, the SARL or its bank (under the RFE delegation) must file the balance-of-payments declaration to the Banque de France via TéléRFE using operation code G2/Capi; (b) the shareholder must evidence source-of-funds at the provider bank; (c) use SWIFT gpi with a UETR for tamper-proof tracking across the correspondent corridor; (d) attach the certified board resolution of the foreign shareholder and the SARL's copy of the executed share-subscription deed; (e) permit the French bank's compliance desk to apply the '135-day' review of the capital source under Article L561-6; (f) do not rely on crypto-bridge rails or third-party omnibus accounts — only the SARL's own blocked IBAN is compliant. The same routing applies to a capital increase, with the additional filing of a formal notarial (if required by the statuts) or signed private deed at the Greffe within one month.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Compliant disbursement rails for a French video-matching SARL: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR (ISO 20022 pain.001.001.03/pacs.008) for supplier invoices under EUR 100,000 within SEPA, settled on TARGET2 same-day or via SEPA Instant for operational payments; (2) SWIFT MT103 / cross-border ISO 20022 pacs.008 for non-EUR payments and non-SEPA counterparties (US cloud providers, foreign content-moderation vendors, Paymentwall settlement accounts), using SWIFT gpi tracking so that each disbursement carries a UETR and achieves end-to-end confirmation; (3) commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) for high-value procurement — e.g., server capacity agreements, licensing of infrastructure, or media-stream processing equipment exceeding EUR 250,000 — issued by the anchor bank on an outright or a revolving basis, with the SARL as applicant and a foreign technology supplier as beneficiary; (4) documentary collections (URC 522) for mid-value payments where LC cost is unjustified; (5) IBAN-to-IBAN direct credits for intra-EU suppliers. Every outbound wire at or above EUR 7,500 is subject to the Banque de France RFE declaration through TéléRFE, with the service/revenue purpose code (e.g., 2S for data-processing services; 3A for licences) indicated; the SARL must also maintain for each disbursement: the underlying commercial contract, a correctly issued invoice, an UBO-awareness check of the payee, sanctions/exclusion-list screening, and — when paying a non-resident licensor of intellectual property — a withholding-tax analysis (use of the applicable France–X double-taxation treaty; at-source 33.33% standard French royalty withholding reduced by treaty, and the French transfer-pricing documentation for related-party IP payments). The Treasury policy must explicitly apply a concentration limit: no single outbound rail may carry more than 40% of monthly vendor value without the gérant's written authorisation, and disbursements to high-risk jurisdictions require second-level compliance approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable outright forward (FXA) — the primary hedge for App Store/Paymentwall USD-denominated revenue against EUR operating costs; executed under an ISDA master agreement (with existing Account); permitted for non-financial counterparties without ACPR licence.
EUR/USD foreign-exchange swap (FXS) — used for short-tenor liquidity management, rolling spot/forward conversion to align USD collection timing with EUR payroll and cloud-invoice dates.

Cross-currency swap (CCS) — permissible for term-matched hedging of USD-denominated infrastructure lease liabilities or a USD-denominated intercompany loan; requires EMIR due-diligence and, if the bank counterparty is a financial counterparty, mandatory clearing or segregation under EMIR thresholds when exceeded.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on exotic settlement currencies (e.g., INR, IDR, BRL, TRY) where Paymentwall conversions expose the SARL to illiquid non-EUR currencies for which the interbank deliverable market is absent or restricted; NDFs are allowed under French law (Code monétaire et financier Art. L452-1 and following) and ACPR/EU-licensed executive counterparties, regulated under EMIR and subject to the SARL's internal hedging policy requiring a minimum correlation of 80% between the notional and the underlying exposure.

Plain-vanilla EUR/USD option collars (zero-cost structures) — permissible but only when the CFO/board has approved the premium budget and when the bank counterparty presents a proper PRIIPS/KID where applicable; options and swaps are prohibited for speculative use under the SARL's treasury charter and must be linked to an identifiable underlying commercial flow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements, management report and auditors' report (if any) – 'Dépôt des comptes annuels'
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via INPI Guichet Unique (RCS Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval required within 6 months of fiscal year-end (June 30 for Dec. 31 year-end); registry filing within 1 month of approval (latest July 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of approximately EUR 200 per notification; directors face a fine up to EUR 7,500; two consecutive years of non-filing allow the public prosecutor to commence RCS strike-off (radiation) and the court may order the mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registration data (K-bis accuracy re-certification) – 'Confirmation annuelle des données'
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet Unique updating the RCS/Greffe record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the 12-monthly anniversary of RCS registration; strict cutoff is the last day of the month following the registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Maintenance of inaccurate official data exposes directors to sanctions for false RCS declarations (up to EUR 30,000 fine); administrative warnings and ex officio rectification proceedings may follow

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return ('Liasse fiscale': form 2065-SD plus 2050-series schedules, balance, P&L, notes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) – Service des impôts des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day after May 1 following the December 31 year-end (typically May 3–4)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 10% increase on income tax due if filed after the notice; graduated to 40%–80% for non-response or dissimulation; monthly late interest of 0.2%; tax assessment can be made ex officio

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration update and annual re-confirmation – 'Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (DBE)'
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (confidential annex to the RCS file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be current whenever the annual confirmation is lodged; re-filed within 30 days of any shareholding/control change (no separate fixed annual date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Up to EUR 7,500 fine for the legal entity and EUR 15,000 for individuals; distributions and share transfers may be blocked while the declaration is defective

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CFE business property levy (annual local business contribution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP (assessed locally; paid via annual notice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: December 15 of the tax year (for the December 31 reference year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late-payment increase plus 0.2% monthly interest; enforced by individual demand notice (avis de recouvrement) without prior assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual electronic-communications operator declaration and IFERC regulatory fee (Real-Time Video Telephony Service)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ARCEP (Autorité de régulation des communications électroniques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual declaration by February 28; fee payable within 30 days of the ARCEP levy notice (Q2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: State enforcement of unpaid IFERC with recovery surcharges; breach of declaration duty exposes the operator to ARCEP censure and administrative fines per the CPCE (up to EUR 70,000)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory 'Commissaire aux comptes' appointment when at least two of three thresholds are exceeded at fiscal year-end: total balance sheet > EUR 4,000,000, revenue (HT) > EUR 8,000,000, average workforce > 50 employees; below these thresholds the SARL is exempt and may only require audit upon shareholder request
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – ANC Regulation 2018-01) for individual statutory accounts; mandatory preservation of books, ledgers and supporting vouchers for 10 years (Code de commerce L.123-22)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For any register change during the year the DBE must be re-lodged within 30 days of the event; the annual K-bis confirmation re-certifies all shareholders exceeding 25% control and any real controlling party, with changes appended in the same filing; non-resident ownership is permissible and must be reflected with passport/ID and residential details
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres / Register of members and share transfers
Registre des décisions sociales / Register of director and shareholder resolutions
Feuilles de présence et procès-verbaux / Minute book and attendance sheets

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 150–EUR 600 (USD 160–650) for commercial domiciliation and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required below mandatory thresholds; EUR 4,000–EUR 12,000 (USD 4,300–13,000) if the statutory audit threshold is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 100% of eligible expenses) and innovation status incentives; no broad tax holidays

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200 - Déclaration de résultat via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g. 30 April for calendar year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, report only French permanent establishment income
Apply 25% rate to taxable profit after adjustments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 0.5% per month of tax due (minimum €125, maximum 25% or €10,000); plus interest and potential criminal sanctions

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate and complete form 2839 via impots.gouv.fr to claim reduced rate under double tax treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 12.8% statutory, reduced to 0-10% under treaties; Interest: 12.8% statutory, reduced to 0-10% under treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) require adequate economic substance in France for tax residency

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to file or understate taxable income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to 80% of evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Imprisonment, fines, and disqualification from corporate roles

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transactions lacking arm's length pricing or missing TP documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 100% of tax adjustment plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Fines and personal liability for willful misconduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining entity without real economic activity or substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization, back taxation, and penalties up to €75,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fines

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to screen cross-border transactions or comply with AML rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 5% of turnover plus criminal penalties
